summary: Tested registration page role removal and dashboard All Orders tab combining orders + consultations. Found 1 backend bug: 'user' role returns empty stats from /api/dashboard/stats.

critical.issue: 'user' role returns empty object {} instead of stats. Backend only handles 'advertiser', 'admin', 'supplier' roles at line 1520 in server.py
critical.fix: Change line 1520 from 'if current_user.role == "advertiser":' to 'if current_user.role in ["user", "advertiser"]:'

action_items: FIX BACKEND BUG: In /app/backend/server.py line 1520, change 'if current_user.role == "advertiser":' to 'if current_user.role in ["user", "advertiser"]:' so that 'user' role gets proper dashboard stats
critical_code_review_comments: Backend server.py line 1520-1625: The dashboard stats endpoint doesn't handle 'user' role - it only handles 'advertiser', 'admin', and 'supplier'. The 'user' role falls through to return {} at line 1625.

User_Dashboard_Stats.description: 'user' role returns empty stats from /api/dashboard/stats - frontend handles gracefully with fallback calculation

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: In server.py line 1520, the dashboard stats endpoint only checks for 'advertiser' role, not 'user' role. The 'user' role falls through all conditions and returns {} at line 1625.
reproduction_steps: 1. Register a new user (gets 'user' role by default)
3. Call GET /api/dashboard/stats with the user's token
4. Response is {} instead of stats object
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Frontend DashboardPage.js handles this gracefully by falling back to manual calculation from orders and consultations arrays when API stats are not available (lines 118-134)
